task.title: Hold the release workflow to the same no-silent-skip bar as CI
task.description:
PR #28 added .github/workflows/ci.yml, which provisions node, runs scripts/check-ci-capabilities.sh as a preflight, sets WORKBOOK_TEST_REQUIRE_CAPABILITIES=1, and pipes the suite through scripts/skipreport. .github/workflows/release.yml was left untouched and still has the exact shape WB-01KZBT4D9E9V7A5A70G1SNHB7W was filed to remove.

.github/workflows/release.yml:38-39 runs a bare 'go test ./...' on ubuntu-24.04 with no actions/setup-node step, no WORKBOOK_TEST_REQUIRE_CAPABILITIES, and no skipreport. If a future runner image drops or relocates node, or the tests move to a node feature the image's version lacks, that step silently skips all 36 internal/webui embedded client behavior tests plus the SHA-256 subtests in internal/gitstore and internal/perf, prints 'ok', and proceeds.

This matters more than it does for the push/PR gate, because the release job is the one that actually builds the darwin and linux archives (scripts/release.sh) and pushes the Homebrew formula (scripts/publish-release.sh). It is the highest-stakes gate in the repo and currently the only one that can ship on a shrunken suite.

Fix is small: add an actions/setup-node step pinned the same way ci.yml pins it, add 'env: WORKBOOK_TEST_REQUIRE_CAPABILITIES: "1"' to the Test step, and optionally reuse scripts/check-ci-capabilities.sh as a preflight so a missing tool fails by name. Consider also routing it through scripts/skipreport for the job summary.

Deferred from PR #28 review as a minor finding: the ticket's acceptance criteria are scoped to the new push/pull-request workflow, all of which that PR meets, so this is a gap in an adjacent workflow rather than an unmet criterion.
